measured: The score is the number of triangles formed by exactly n straight lines that no other line of the arrangement cuts through (bounded triangular faces). Higher is better. A submission is a solution.json listing the lines as integer triples [a, b, c] meaning a·x + b·y + c = 0; the hill's evaluator counts the triangles with exact rational arithmetic, so there is no tolerance and no randomness. It stands in for a real, checkable geometric construction for the Kobon triangle problem. Different line counts are separate contests. Nothing is held out from the construction itself; the hill's only private data are regression fixtures for its own tests, which were not shipped to us and were not read. All runs are on this machine (local, 24 CPU cores); hardware is not part of the score.

SAT model for SIMPLE pseudoline arrangements (search/kobon_sat.py): one sign per triple of lines (816 for 18 lines) plus the 4-line consistency rule. The triangle rule was derived from 20,000 real 4-line arrangements (search/signotope4.py) and reproduces the exact evaluator on real arrangements (93, 65, 16).

Validation against known values: finds the record and rules out record+1 for n = 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 (10 lines: 26 ruled out in 27 s). For n = 8 it rules out 15, yet 15 is the proven optimum: the gallery's 8-line 15 uses 2 triple crossings. So simple arrangements top out at 14 for 8 lines.

Clue from the gallery certificates: every known even-n record uses triple crossings (6: 3, 8: 2, 10: 7, 12: 4, 14: 5, 16: 3, 20: 6); the odd 17-line 85 has none. Consequences: (1) a proof that 94 is impossible must cover arrangements with triple crossings; (2) the unseeded annealer cannot create triple crossings, so it is blind to the kind of arrangement that wins at even n.
Parallel lines never need encoding: a projective map sending a generic far-away line to infinity keeps every bounded triangle and makes all slopes distinct.

LITERATURE (subagent review): for SIMPLE arrangements 93 is already proven optimal at 18 lines (Blanc, arXiv 0801.2845: even n gives at most floor(n(n-5/2)/3), which is 93). Wikipedia's 94 is the older Bartholdi-Blanc-Loisel bound, which is also only for simple arrangements. So a 94 needs a point where 3 or more lines meet; for that case only 95 (Clement-Bader, informal) and 96 (Tamura) are known. No 18-line SAT attempt is published. The ud1 gallery has about 3,000 distinct 93s for 18 lines (up to 8 triple points) and no 94.

Counting identity (from the review): 3T = n(n-2) - Lambda, where Lambda = unused segments - doubly used segments + sum over multiple points of k(k-2). So 94 at 18 lines means Lambda <= 6; every known 93 has Lambda = 9. Search hint: record arrangements put their triple points on one line; a 94 would need clustered triple points joined by segments shared by two triangles.

Triple-crossing SAT model (3-valued signs, 17 realizable 4-line patterns derived empirically) validated: finds 15 for 8 lines (2 triple points) and rules out 16 in 3.7 s. The proof pipeline works end to end: CaDiCaL wrote a 10 MB DRAT proof for that case, verified by drat-trim.

Timing with the old models: proofs stall at 10-11 lines (10 lines/26 not settled in 15 min; 11/33 not in 20 min, while Savchuk's encoding does it in 1.7 s). Finding is slow too (13/47 simple in 10 min; 11/32 with triple points in 8 min). This is the user's case 4.

Defect-budget model (search/kobon_sat.py --defect K): adds each line's explicit crossing order (point i before j on line r iff sign(sorted r,i,j) = -1, derived empirically) and consecutive-pair variables. It then caps "consecutive pair that is not a triangle side" at n(n-2) + 6K - 3T, a valid bound for arrangements with at most K triple points and no 4-fold point. Validated: 8/15 found with 2 triple points, ruled out with 0 (1.1 s); 8/16 ruled out with up to 2 (6 s); 9/22 ruled out with up to 1 (12.9 s).

Improved defect model: tighter budget n(n-2) + 3k + C(k,2) - 3T (two triple points share at most one line), plus rotation symmetry breaking (line 0 is defect-free; it also avoids triple points when enough lines remain). Still finds the real 8-line 15. Timings: 11/33 simple 3.3 s (old models: unsolved in 20+ min; Savchuk: 1.7 s); 10/26 simple 5.4 s; 10/26 with <=1 triple point 37 s; 10/26 with <=2: 379 s; 12/39 simple (budget 3): 534 s.

Checkable proofs: search/cnc.py (march_cu cubes, CaDiCaL + DRAT per cube, drat-trim check, plus a coverage proof that the cubes cover everything). 10 lines, 26 triangles, <=1 triple point: 190 cubes plus coverage, all UNSAT and all verified.

Scaling verdict (user's case 4): solve time grows steeply with the defect budget; 18 lines needs budget 6 (no triple points, i.e. Blanc's theorem again), 9 (<=1) and 13 (<=2). A single solver likely needs days, so a full proof does not fit in hours with this encoding. Next: borrow faster tooling from the literature (Parpalak-Utkin word search, Savchuk kobon-cnf, the ud1 generators); a code review is running.

None of these tools exhaustively covers 18 lines with triple points.

NEW PARTIAL RESULT (subagent's extend_dp.py, an exact longest-path DP over all ways to add one pseudoline, triple points included; validated against exhaustive enumeration at n=9 and against known optima 25, 54, 72): extending any of the 255 perfect 17-line wiring diagrams gives at most 93. So no 18-line 94 becomes a perfect 17 when one line is deleted. That class holds 291 of 500 sampled gallery 93s, with all their triple points on the added line. Independent check here: best 18th line through two crossing points of the gallery's real 17/85 is 93 (1 line), never 94.
Regression check (subagent): the chi derived from about 1,500 gallery arrangements (n = 12, 14, 18, 20) satisfies our 17 patterns, the before-rule, the triangle rule and the pair bound. No failures.

SOUNDNESS REGRESSION (search/regress_real.py): exact gallery certificates with triple points, rotated exactly (rational rotation) so the symmetry-broken line 0 is legal, then their chi fixed as units in the defect CNF. All satisfiable: 8/15 (2 triple points), 10/25 (7), 12/38 (4), 14/54 (5), 16/72 (3), 18/93 (3), 20/117 (6), plus our simple 18/93. (A first run flagged 3 failures; the cause was the harness not applying the 180-degree sign flip that the model's symmetry clause assumes, not a model bug.)

Base + 2 free lines (search/base2.py): a gallery base on n-2 lines is fixed through solver assumptions at each of the 153 slope-position pairs; the 256 triples involving the new lines stay free and 3-valued. Self-test: deleting 2 lines of a real 18/93 and asking for 93 at the true positions is SAT; the same base at 94 is UNSAT (22 s).

GPU: not useful here. SAT and the exact DP are branch-heavy serial searches, and the only GPU-friendly search (float annealing) produces only simple arrangements, where 93 is already proven optimal (Blanc). A GPU would help only to straighten a SAT-found candidate.

GALLERY SWEEP (work/research2/extend_dp.py, exact optimal one-line re-insertion, triple points allowed): all 3,016 gallery 18-line 93s (with and without parallel pairs, 0-8 triple points), each of the 18 lines deleted and re-inserted optimally: 54,288 cases, maximum exactly 93 in every case. No known 93 is one line away from a 94.

Base + 2 free lines on one gallery 16/72 (first file in gallery/data/16): target 94 is UNSAT at all 153 slope-position pairs (pysat/CaDiCaL, no DRAT yet), 2,607 s on one core (median 16 s per pair). All 914 gallery 72s would take about 660 core-hours, roughly a day on this laptop.

Split proof: 12 lines/38 simple, split by hand on the signs of 8 triples (1,2,j) into 256 cases plus coverage. Cases take 3-19 s each with DRAT verified; the last and hardest one is still being checked.
18/94 single-solver SAT runs (K = 0, 1, 2 triple points): no answer within their 90-minute limit.

parpalak/kobon-solutions fork: one commit ahead of ud1 ("add certs for 18, 22, 53, 54"). The 18-line certificate is a 93 with 4 triple points (Z=5, D=8), coefficients up to 22 digits. It passes the hill's evaluator (93) and the soundness regression, and its source word was already covered by the sweep.

FEASIBILITY (work/sample_cubes.py): the 18/94 defect CNF with <= 1 triple point has budget 9, 199,162 vars and 818,121 clauses. Random cubes over the signs of triples (1,2,j),(1,3,j): m=12 gave 8/8 timeouts at 480 s; m=16 gave 6/8 timeouts and 2 trivial UNSAT (0.5 s). Estimated at least 65,536 x 360 s = 23.6M core-seconds. Not feasible; proof track closed.

NEW SOUND CONSTRAINT (opposite-sides rule): if consecutive segments [P_i,P_j] and [P_j,P_l] of line r are both triangle sides on the same side of r, both triangles use the first segment of line j's ray from P_j, so their apexes coincide (i, j, l concurrent). So same side implies chi(i,j,l) = 0. Added as --alternate; the soundness regression still passes on 9 real arrangements (0-7 triple points).

Solver/encoding matrix (16 runs in parallel): 12/39 simple went from CaDiCaL baseline 351 s to Kissat + opposite-sides + totalizer 193 s; 10/26 with <=2 triple points went from CaDiCaL (pysat) 379 s to Kissat + opposite-sides + counting network 210 s. So about 2x, far short of the 10-100x needed. The totalizer blows up at 18 lines (13.5M clauses), so the counting network is used there (913k clauses).

Split strategy: cubes = the first 3 lines crossed along line 0 (4,080 cubes; complete, since every crossing order has a prefix). With Kissat, 8 of 14 sampled 18/94 (<=1 triple point) cubes were UNSAT within 8 min (0.3-158 s) and 6 timed out, versus 0 of 8 at 4,096 random-sign cubes. Rough estimate 1-2 days on 24 cores (uncertain: the timeouts' true cost is unknown).

kobon-cnf (Savchuk): table encoding, simple arrangements only (rows are full permutations), so it cannot express the triple points a 94 needs. Its ideas (Kissat, local per-line structure) are already in the defect model. On 11/33 it takes 1.7 s versus 3.3 s for ours, so it is not dramatically faster.
Exactly-K option (--exact): the "at most 1 triple point" question splits into 0 (Blanc's published theorem) and exactly 1 (new), so only the latter needs a proof.

Mirror symmetry derived exactly (work/mirror_rule.py, 9 checks on 3 arrangements): reflecting across line 0 keeps line 0's crossing order and relabels i -> n-i. Combined with the 180-degree normalization it pairs cubes only in half the space (about 1.3x), so it is not used.
Kissat modes: --unsat (stable=0) is available; not benchmarked because of time pressure (the user asked to go straight to the full run).

THEOREM (hand proof; see SUMMARY.md): with exactly one triple point P and no parallels, 3T = 285 - Z + D. D <= 2: a doubly used segment is the first segment of a ray at P, and needs one "cap line" crossing three consecutive rays first; such blocks are disjoint. Every clean line (avoids P, not a cap line) claims an unused segment by Blanc's alternation/parity argument (18 - 3 is odd), and each unused segment is claimed at most twice. So Z >= ceil((15 - D)/2), Z - D >= 5, and T <= 93. Found by subagent (work/blanc/); every step re-derived here; 0 counterexamples on 7,264 exact perturbations.

Two triple points: the same counting forces the two points to share no line (otherwise Z >= 5 > D), D = 4, Z = 4, 4 distinct cap lines and 8 clean lines whose claims pair up exactly. Encoded in kobon_sat.py as --blanc (the claims; sound for every even-n arrangement with only triple points; the soundness regression passes on 9 real arrangements) and --k2-18 (the deductions for n=18, T=94, exactly 2).

CORRECTION (21:25Z): an earlier note said the two triple points must share no line. Wrong: they may be consecutive on a common line with the segment PQ a side of two triangles (D = Z = 5, 9 clean lines). The --k2-18 deductions are therefore valid for case A only (code and SUMMARY fixed); no conclusion had been drawn from them.

Two-triple-point SAT test (Blanc claims + case-A deductions; 271k vars, 1.06M clauses): the whole instance timed out at 600 s (Kissat default and --unsat), and 16 of 20 random line-0 cubes timed out at 600 s. Not closable quickly.
Generalization checked by hand: exactly one triple point, even n: 3T <= n(n-2) - 3 - (n-8)/2, i.e. T <= floor((2n^2 - 5n + 2)/6).
Two-triple-point run v1 (21:29-21:39Z, 240 s limit): case A 96 UNSAT / 22 timeouts, case B 92 / 22, in 10 min; projected about 80 h per case, with timeouts using about 3/4 of the compute.

Extra deductions (both cases): every segment at a triple point is used (the two cap blocks cover all 6 rays), so unused segments have simple endpoints and the Blanc claims total at most 2Z (8 in A, 10 in B). Case B has at least 5 triangles at each triple point. Encoded; v2 restarted with a 60 s split limit.

REFEREE REPORT (work/referee/): L1, L3, L4, the stretch lemma and the counting are correct; the original L2 disjointness was wrong in case B (blocks can overlap on the ray between P and Q; explicit examples at n = 10, 16, 18), and the patch and a simpler case-B argument (x >= 2) both hold. Theorem G is correct. Tested on 142,160 arrangements: 321,793 doubly used segments, 315,797 blocks, 4.79M even stretches, 68,830 valid axes, 1.62M clean lines; no counterexamples. Two false case-B statements in SUMMARY.md and the --case2 B SAT deductions were corrected.
ud1 kobon.cpp (heuristic DFS, its original pruning) at 18/94: finished 22:02Z, 843,312,536,903 iterations, 0 arrangements found. Its shortcut prunes are unsound, so this is evidence only.
